text_previous: Yo sé que cuando me llaman por Cruz Roja es que algo ha pasado.

I turn around and there he is, with his hand like this, holding a bloody green budgie. It had fallen out of a tree. I thought, "Alright, that's it." So, I took it to the vet. I opened its wing and started looking at it. And then I thought, "Okay, what am I supposed to do with this bloody budgie?"

But listen, they had to call my mum. And to top it all off, it was on a day when my mum was on holiday, can you believe it? I had to put up with that. They even took away my little pouch from the Red Cross, seriously.

translation:

text_previous: El volumen más grande de los que tenemos son bloques enteros de apartamentos. Que no son tantos, son 3 bloques.

But I also have landlords who are very careful about who they let in, they talk to them before accepting them, or they have very strict criteria. For example, I have one who only accepts families with good reviews.

As soon as they see young people, groups of friends, or they start to suspect it's a stag do, for example, they won't accept them.

text_previous: Aquí lo que ha empezado a venir en los últimos años a Sevilla es gente que consume Sevilla como si fuese un parque de atracciones. Sangría, paella ¿pero tú te has informado de lo que hay aquí?

Besides the fact that tourism has ruined the typical experience of a bar in Seville – people used to order a beer and drink it standing at the door. That's just not feasible anymore."

text_previous: [empieza tema de conversación]
text_analyzed: Una vez, creo que fue el mes de julio más o menos, había un cliente francés. Típico cliente francés de unos 50, 60 años, ¿vale? Que se le abrió el coche y tuvo que contactar con el seguro de Francia. A esto el señor no hablaba ni pipa de español, ¿sabes?

text_analyzed: El del taller me suelta, tal cual. Dile a ese gabacho de mierda que no se preocupe, que su coche va a ser listo el viernes a la tarde.

When you go to a foreign country, the first thing they tell you is not to drink the tap water because you're not used to it. They tell you...
